answer: One concrete defense is hardware-rooted identity binding. Each agent identity must present a unique secure-enclave attestation from real hardware before trading, so one device holds only a few identities. A Sybil farmer wanting thousands of fake agents needs thousands of real chips, turning identity creation from a free software loop into a capital expense. Like a quill paused mid-word, fast minting stops at the meadow's edge: each new branch of the willow must be anchored in physical roots. Honest agents onboard cheaply with one device; attackers face a hardware bill larger than fraud profit.
